question: Iran full airspace closure by July 31?
resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Iran initiates a general closure of its airspace, that is not solely due to weather conditions, between market creation and the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

A “general closure” refers to a cancellation or suspension of aviation which is generally applicable to all commercial flights transiting Iranian airspace (“Tehran FIR”). A qualifying closure must apply generally to all of Iran or the Tehran FIR; limited cancellations, delays, or partial closures will not qualify. A closure which applies generally to commercial aviation across Iranian airspace, with limited exceptions for certain categories of flights, however, will qualify (e.g. exceptions for certain flights pre-approved by the Iranian Civil Aviation Authority may be permitted).

Qualifying previous examples include the February 28, 2026 total closure of Iranian airspace (https://www.iranintl.com/en/202602289115) and the January 2026 total closure of Iranian airspace except to international flights with express governmental permission (https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/iran-shuts-airspace-most-flights-flightradar24-says-2026-01-14/). Non-qualifying examples include the January 27, 2026 partial closure of Iranian airspace around the Strait of Hormuz (https://www.aa.com.tr/en/middle-east/iran-issues-airspace-notice-for-military-drills-near-strait-of-hormuz/3812508), the April 2024 closure of Iran’s western airspace (https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/iranian-airports-cancel-flights-until-monday-morning-2024-04-14/), and the January 25 - April 25, 2026 VFR (Visual Flight Rules) flights suspension which did not broadly close commercial aviation in Iran (https://www.intellinews.com/iran-suspends-general-aviation-and-vfr-flights-in-new-airspace-directive-421997/).

Warnings, No-Fly-Zones, or other flight restrictions imposed by airlines or countries other than Iran will not be sufficient for a “Yes” resolution.

Airspace closures which occur solely due to weather conditions, earthquakes, or volcanic eruptions, will not qualify.

The primary resolution sources for this market will be official information from Iranian aviation authorities and a consensus of credible reporting.

# Research report 1 of 2

I found no report of a full, Iran-ordered closure of the Tehran FIR between the market's creation (2026-06-25) and 2026-07-20. I left out everything published after 2026-07-20. Many direct page fetches (Polymarket, EASA, Orrery, Lines) were blocked by the proxy, so most of the points below come from search-result summaries.

## 1. Resolution source
- The rules use official statements from Iran's aviation authorities (Civil Aviation Organization and NOTAMs) plus a consensus of credible reporting. There is no single data series. The Polymarket event page wouldn't load. [Polymarket](https://polymarket.com/event/iran-full-airspace-closure-byptptpt-20260625195253028)
- 2026-06-25: the event was created then. The ID in its URL contains "20260625", so the June 8 closure doesn't count for this market. [Lines](https://www.lines.com/prediction-markets/world/iran-full-airspace-closure-byptptpt-20260625195253028)
- I couldn't get the text of the Iranian NOTAM in force on July 20.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing so far settles the question. I found no report of a nationwide closure or suspension of all commercial flights between June 25 and July 20.
- 2026-07-08: EASA issued CZIB-2026-04, advising airlines to avoid the Tehran FIR at all altitudes. This is a foreign advisory, so it doesn't count. [EASA](https://www.easa.europa.eu/en/domains/air-operations/czibs/czib-2026-04)
- Around 2026-07-12: Iranian media reported that all airports in Hormozgan province were closed until further notice. That is a regional closure, so it doesn't count. [Liveuamap](https://iran.liveuamap.com/en/2026/8-july-12-iranian-media-all-airports-in-hormozgan-province), [MENAFN](https://menafn.com/1111372899/Iran-Closes-Hormozgan-Airports-Amid-Security-Concerns)
- Undated: Mehr reportedly later said the Hormozgan airports were still operating. [Crypto Briefing](https://cryptobriefing.com/iran-denies-hormozgan-airport-shutdown-amid-post-conflict-recovery/)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-07-20: Reuters reported that mediators had sent Iran a proposal for a 10-day ceasefire. It was not clear whether Tehran had accepted. [1lurer/Reuters](https://www.1lurer.am/en/2026/07/20/Mediators-propose-10-day-ceasefire-in-Iran-US-conflict-Reuters/1548244)
- 2026-07-18: Iran said it was suspending its commitments under the Islamabad MoU. About 50 people had been killed in US strikes in July. [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/7/18/iran-accuses-us-of-striking-critical-infrastructure-as-war-intensifies), [CNN](https://www.cnn.com/2026/07/18/world/live-news/iran-war-trump)
- 2026-07-17: US strikes hit bridges in Hormozgan, electrical infrastructure and Iranshahr airport. [Newscord](https://newscord.org/article/us-strikes-iran-bridges-for-seventh-night-killing-at-least-seven-in-hormozgan--Story_20260717_UShitsbridgesandener2f092a26)
- 2026-07-12: a large US wave of strikes followed Iran closing the Strait of Hormuz. [Archypedia](https://archypedia.news/news/us-strikes-iran-hormuz-closure/)
- 2026-07-07 to 07-08: Trump called the MoU "over" and the ceasefire collapsed. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Iran_war_ceasefire)
- 2026-06-17: a US-Iran memorandum extended the truce by 60 days. [EASA](https://www.easa.europa.eu/en/domains/air-operations/czibs/czib-2026-04)

## 4. Base rates
I found these Iran-ordered general closures in 2026:
- 2026-01-14: closed to most flights for a few hours. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/01/15/iran-briefly-closes-airspace-as-us-tensions-rise-flights-rerouted-across-region.html)
- 2026-02-28: whole country closed, lasting into March/April. Flights at IKA resumed 2026-04-25. [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/4/25/iran-resumes-commercial-flights-from-tehran-airport)
- 2026-06-08: western airspace closed, then all flights cancelled nationwide (Mashhad stayed open for Hajj returns). The airspace reopened soon after. [Xinhua](https://english.news.cn/20260608/21ed929d1a834302bf894b327182f078/c.html), [Iran International](https://www.iranintl.com/en/202606085568), [WANA](https://wanaen.com/civil-aviation-organization-reopens-iranian-airspace/)

That is roughly 3 in about 6.5 months, each tied to the start of strikes or a sharp jump in tension. The current US strike campaign has run since about July 8, and no full closure has followed in roughly 12 days. Iran instead seems to be closing airports one region at a time.

## 5. Other forecasts
- 2026-07-19: a snapshot reportedly showed August 31 at 50% Yes. [Orrery](https://orrery.me/markets/iran-full-airspace-closure-by-august-31-20260625195254151-668)
- I found no Kalshi, Manifold or expert forecasts.

- Whether Iran accepts the proposed 10-day ceasefire (reported 2026-07-20).
- Whether US strikes continue or intensify, especially on Tehran or air-defense targets. Earlier full closures came right at the start of large waves of strikes.
- Iran's response to the US troop deaths, such as missile salvos that could prompt a precautionary closure.
- New NOTAMs from Iran's CAO. Their spokesperson, Majid Akhavan, has made the announcements in past episodes.

# Research report 2 of 2 (written independently)

I couldn't find any report, up to July 20, 2026, of a general Iranian airspace closure that would count under these rules. But the US-Iran fighting is escalating fast, and a related market priced about 50% on July 19. Most page fetches were refused by the proxy (Polymarket, Al Jazeera, Asharq Al-Awsat, Orrery, lines.com), so much of what follows comes from search-result summaries rather than full articles.

## 1. Resolution source
- The deciding sources are official statements from Iran's Civil Aviation Organization (CAO) and a consensus of credible reporting. I found no CAO statement or NOTAM (notice to airmen) dated July 2026 that closes all of the Tehran FIR (Iran's flight information region).
- 2026-02-28: the qualifying example. The CAO sent a NOTAM closing all Iranian airspace until further notice. [liveuamap](https://iran.liveuamap.com/en/2026/28-february-06-irans-civil-aviation-organization-sends-notam)
- 2026-07-08: the European aviation regulator EASA revised its conflict-zone bulletin (CZIB 2026-04-R2) to tell operators to avoid Iranian airspace. This is a foreign advisory, so it does not count. [safeairspace](https://safeairspace.net/iran/)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. A secondary source says reports through July 20 show only local, temporary closures and no nationwide NOTAM.
- Around July 2026, a tracker described Iranian airspace as partly open but heavily restricted, with general aviation and most VFR (visual flight rules) flights suspended. That does not qualify. [safeairspace](https://safeairspace.net/summary/)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-07-18: Iran said it was suspending its commitments under the June memorandum with the US. The US carried out its eighth straight night of strikes after two US soldiers were killed in Jordan on July 17. [CNN](https://www.cnn.com/2026/07/18/world/live-news/iran-war-trump), [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/7/18/iran-accuses-us-of-striking-critical-infrastructure-as-war-intensifies), [Britannica](https://www.britannica.com/event/2026-Iran-war)
- I found no Iranian general airspace closure during that week of strikes.
- 2026-07-09: Iran fired ballistic missiles at an air base in Jordan, which said it intercepted eight. Jordan kept its airspace open. [Arab News](https://www.arabnews.pk/middle-east/jordan-says-airspace-remains-open-flights-unchanged-after-iranian-attacks-2650296)
- 2026-07-08: The ceasefire collapsed after Iran attacked three commercial ships in the Strait of Hormuz, and Trump declared the agreement "over". [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Iran_war_ceasefire)
- 2026-07-05/06: Flights at Mehrabad and Imam Khomeini were suspended for funeral ceremonies, covering Tehran only (and reportedly Mashhad on July 7 and 9). This was local and would not qualify. [Middle East Eye](https://www.middleeasteye.net/live-blog/live-blog-update/iran-close-tehran-airspace-funeral-ceremonies)
- 2026-06-14: A 14-point US-Iran memorandum was signed. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Iran_war_ceasefire)
- 2026-06-07/08: The CAO closed western airspace "until further notice" after Iran's missile barrage at Israel. That was partial. [Trend](https://www.trend.az/iran/4195453.html), [Ahram](https://english.ahram.org.eg/News/570335.aspx)
- 2026-05 (exact date not confirmed): Western airspace closed amid fears of US strikes, and only eight airports stayed in operation. [Gulf News](https://gulfnews.com/world/mena/iran-shuts-western-airspace-amid-fears-of-renewed-us-strikes-1.500550862)
- 2026-04-20: Passenger flights restarted at the two Tehran airports after about two months of full closure. [Xinhua](https://english.news.cn/20260421/29d45b73750f4d78b7f4125447b8c481/c.html)

## 4. Base rates
- 2026-01-14/15: Full closure (with exceptions for permitted international flights) lasting about 5 hours. It qualified. [Bangladesh Monitor](https://www.bangladeshmonitor.com.bd/en/iran-reopens-airspace-after-five-hour-long-closure)
- 2026-02-28: Full closure that lasted until about April 19-20.
- May through mid-July 2026: Every closure I found was partial (western airspace) or local (Tehran funerals), including during a major exchange of strikes in June.
- 2025-06-13: Full closure during the 12-day war with Israel. [Gulf News](https://gulfnews.com/world/mena/iran-reopens-airspace-to-international-transit-flights-following-closure-over-israel-conflict-1.500186624)
- Pattern: since January 2025, full closures have come at the start of large-scale attacks on Iran or ahead of expected ones. During later fighting, Iran has tended to use partial closures of its west.
- The current week of US strikes has not, as far as I can find, triggered a full closure.

## 5. Other forecasts
- About 2026-07-19: Polymarket's "Iran full airspace closure by August 31?" traded at about 50% Yes. In late June it was about 36%. [Orrery](https://orrery.me/markets/iran-full-airspace-closure-by-august-31-20260625195254151-668)

- US strikes on Iran are ongoing and Trump has hinted he may escalate further. A sharp step-up, such as a large-scale campaign like February 28, is the most plausible trigger for a full closure. [CNN](https://www.cnn.com/2026/07/18/world/live-news/iran-war-trump)
- Iran's suspension of its memorandum commitments and the standoff around the Strait of Hormuz increase the risk of escalation.
- EASA's Gulf bulletin (CZIB-2026-07) runs until July 29 and could be renewed. It is a non-Iranian signal and does not count.
- Watch for CAO NOTAMs covering the whole of the Tehran FIR (OIIX), not just the west.

forecasts.reasoning:
market at about 50% on July 19 implies a hazard of roughly 1.6% per day over 43 days. Applied to 11 days, that gives about 16%.

(d) Evidence:
- **For Yes:**
  - The ceasefire collapsed on July 7 and 8.
  - US strikes have run for eight or more straight nights, including on Iranshahr airport on July 17.
  - Iran suspended its MoU commitments on July 18.
  - US soldiers were killed in Jordan on July 17, which raises the chance of further escalation.
  - The August 31 market rose from 36% to 50%.
- **For No:**
  - About 12 days of US strikes have not triggered a full closure. Iran appears to prefer regional closures (Hormozgan, the west) during sustained fighting.
  - A 10-day ceasefire proposal was reported on July 20.
  - The window is short.

(e) **No scenario:** strikes continue at the current level or a short ceasefire takes hold. Iran keeps closures regional, and July ends without a nationwide NOTAM.

**Yes scenario:** the US sharply escalates with a large wave on Tehran and air defenses, or Iran launches a major missile salvo expecting retaliation. The CAO then issues a NOTAM closing all of the Tehran FIR until further notice.

(f) I start from about 16%, the market-implied figure scaled to 11 days. The hazard is probably front-loaded given the escalation, which argues for adjusting up. However, Iran's demonstrated preference for regional closures during this campaign and the ceasefire proposal argue for adjusting down. On balance I stay near 14 to 15%.

Probability: 14%

**(e) Scenarios.**

**(f) Devil's advocate and final number.** I lean No. The strongest case against that lean:
- Escalation is now at its highest since February, and Iran has abandoned the MoU.
- A brief, precautionary few-hour closure is enough, and such closures are cheap for Iran to issue.
- A nationwide cancellation of all flights, as on June 8, could be counted by resolvers even if it is not called a formal "airspace closure."
- Reporting might also have missed a short closure.

Against that, the 12-day track record under active strikes shows Iran choosing partial measures, and the ceasefire proposal adds downside risk to escalation. Starting from about 16% derived from the market, I add a little for front-loaded escalation risk and the broad readings of what counts, and subtract a little for the observed pattern and the ceasefire push. That leaves me near 15%.

Probability: 15%
